rv.q: I loved every minute that Severo was on stage, and believe that anyone else attending Frida… A Self Portrait will too.
In this evocative portrait of Frida Kahlo, art becomes more than a reflection of life; it gives lasting form to the love, longing, and memories that continue to inhabit us.
Another highlight of an outstanding performance is how she conveys Frida as a woman accustomed to pain who is, at the end of her life, suddenly pushed into agony even she thought impossible.
Both playwright and performer, Vanessa Severo (Frida Kahlo) is simply astonishing in this production.

Severo’s 75-minute pulsating one-woman show (she plays herself, Kahlo, and assorted others) is built around a smart framing device involving a fictional visit from a journalist with an architecture magazine.
If you are a connoisseur of great acting, then by all means see this play.
